key_terms.meaning: DC input voltage where V<sub>out</sub> = V<sub>in</sub>; near V<sub>DD</sub>/2 for a symmetric CMOS inverter.
NM<sub>H</sub> = V<sub>OH</sub> − V<sub>IH</sub> and NM<sub>L</sub> = V<sub>IL</sub> − V<sub>OL</sub>; allowed voltage disturbance at a logic input.
Enhancement nMOS driver with a resistor pull-up; output low depends on the resistance ratio and static current flows in the low state.
Enhancement nMOS load with gate tied to V<sub>DD</sub>; output high is limited to about V<sub>DD</sub> − V<sub>t</sub>.
Depletion nMOS pull-up with V<sub>GS</sub> = 0; gives a better high level and faster pull-up than an enhancement load.
Always-on pMOS pull-up with gate at ground and an nMOS pull-down network; ratioed, with static current when the output is low.
t<sub>p</sub> = (t<sub>pHL</sub> + t<sub>pLH</sub>)/2, measured from the 50% input point to the 50% output point.
Ratio of a gate input capacitance to that of an inverter with the same output current; gate delay is d = gh + p.
Intrinsic delay of a gate driving no external load, expressed in logical-effort delay units.
P<sub>dyn</sub> = α C<sub>L</sub> V<sub>DD</sub><sup>2</sup> f, where α is the activity factor, C<sub>L</sub> is load capacitance, V<sub>DD</sub> is supply voltage and f is clock frequency.
Power from current that flows from V<sub>DD</sub> to ground during an input transition while nMOS and pMOS are both on.
Drain-to-source current when V<sub>GS</sub> is below V<sub>t</sub>; it grows exponentially with temperature and lower V<sub>t</sub>.
Switching off a block with high-V<sub>t</sub> header or footer transistors to cut leakage when the block is idle.
Complementary pMOS pull-up and nMOS pull-down networks; rail-to-rail output and no steady-state current for a valid input.
An always-on load fights a pull-down network; the low output depends on the strength ratio and static current flows.
MOS switch that connects an input to an output; a single nMOS passes 0 strongly but a 1 only up to about V<sub>DD</sub> − V<sub>t</sub>.
nMOS and pMOS in parallel with complementary gate signals; passes full 0 and full 1 levels.
Clocked logic that precharges the output and then evaluates by conditionally discharging it; the output is not held indefinitely.
Dynamic gate followed by an inverter so cascaded stages can only discharge in the evaluate phase, preventing false evaluation.
Cascode voltage switch logic; a cross-coupled pMOS pair acts as a latch in the pull-up and produces differential outputs.

takeaways: The CMOS inverter voltage transfer curve has five regions, and its switching threshold is the input where output equals input.
Noise margins come from V<sub>IL</sub>, V<sub>IH</sub>, V<sub>OL</sub> and V<sub>OH</sub>; a symmetric inverter gives the widest margins.
An NMOS inverter needs a load, and the resistive, enhancement, depletion and pseudo-nMOS choices trade output levels, static current and speed.
Propagation delay is set by charging and discharging load capacitance through the finite drive current of the transistors.
Logical effort estimates multistage path delay and shows how to size each stage for minimum delay.
CMOS power is dynamic, short-circuit and leakage power; dynamic power dominates when switching and leakage dominates when idle.
Low-power design lowers activity, capacitance and supply voltage, and cuts leakage with power gating or high-V<sub>t</sub> devices.
Static CMOS is robust; ratioed, pass-transistor and dynamic styles save area or transistors but add static current, voltage loss, clocking or charge-sharing problems.
bank_note: Long answers usually compare logic styles on DC levels, static current, delay, area and power, and ask for delay or power calculations using logical effort, capacitance and supply voltage.

bank.q: Draw the voltage transfer characteristic of a CMOS inverter and explain its five regions. Define V<sub>IL</sub>, V<sub>IH</sub>, V<sub>OL</sub>, V<sub>OH</sub>, V<sub>M</sub> and both noise margins.
outline: definitions of V<sub>IL</sub>, V<sub>IH</sub>, V<sub>OL</sub>, V<sub>OH</sub> and V<sub>M</sub>
symmetric inverter has V<sub>M</sub> near V<sub>DD</sub>/2

bank.q: Compare resistive-load, enhancement-load, depletion-load and pseudo-nMOS NMOS inverters on output low voltage, output high voltage, static current and speed.
outline: output low level and ratio dependence

bank.q: Explain how load capacitance and transistor on-resistance set the propagation delay of a CMOS inverter. Define t<sub>pHL</sub>, t<sub>pLH</sub>, t<sub>p</sub>, rise time and fall time.
Explain logical effort, electrical effort, parasitic delay and path effort. Show how they produce a path delay estimate for a multistage logic path.
outline: stage sizing from best stage effort

bank.q: List the components of power dissipation in CMOS circuits and write one formula for each.
outline: dependence on V<sub>DD</sub>, f, activity and temperature
difference between active and standby power

bank.q: Explain subthreshold, gate-oxide and junction leakage in CMOS. Describe power gating and high-V<sub>t</sub> device use as remedies.
outline: power gating with headers or footers
cost in area, delay and state retention

bank.q: For a symmetric CMOS inverter with V<sub>DD</sub> = 3.3 V, V<sub>tn</sub> = 0.7 V and V<sub>tp</sub> = −0.7 V, estimate V<sub>M</sub> and the logic swing. State your assumptions.
outline: set nMOS and pMOS currents equal
V<sub>M</sub> = 1.65 V for the symmetric case
logic swing from 0 V to 3.3 V
state that mobility and size assumptions matter

bank.q: A three-stage path has stage 1: g = 1, h = 4, p = 1; stage 2: g = 5/3, h = 3, p = 2; stage 3: g = 4/3, h = 2, p = 1. Calculate each stage delay and the total path delay.
outline: stage delay formula d = gh + p

bank.q: A CMOS chip has 1 million switching nodes, average load capacitance 20 fF per node, V<sub>DD</sub> = 1.2 V, activity factor 0.2 and clock frequency 500 MHz. Calculate the dynamic power.
outline: use P = α C V<sub>DD</sub><sup>2</sup> f
state that this excludes short-circuit and leakage power

bank.q: Compare static CMOS, ratioed logic, pass-transistor logic and transmission-gate logic for a 2:1 multiplexer. Discuss output levels, transistor count, static current and delay.
outline: static CMOS full levels and no static current
ratioed logic fewer transistors but static current
nMOS pass transistor loses V<sub>t</sub> on high level

bank.q: Explain why a single nMOS pass transistor cannot pass a full V<sub>DD</sub> high level. Show how a transmission gate fixes this and discuss charge sharing and body-effect problems.
outline: nMOS passes high level only to V<sub>DD</sub> − V<sub>t</sub>
parallel transmission gate passes both rails
charge sharing with floating output nodes

bank.q: Describe the precharge and evaluate phases of dynamic logic. Explain clock feedthrough, charge sharing and why domino logic is needed for cascades; include CVSL.
outline: domino inverter blocks false high-to-low cascade
CVSL cross-coupled pMOS latch and differential outputs

bank.q: A low-power datapath must trade speed, area, static current and leakage. Evaluate static CMOS, ratioed, pass-transistor, transmission-gate and dynamic styles, and recommend sizing and power-management steps.
outline: static CMOS robustness and no static current
ratioed and pseudo-nMOS static current penalty
pass-transistor and transmission-gate area and level issues
dynamic logic clocking and charge-sharing risk
lower V<sub>DD</sub>, lower activity, power gating and high-V<sub>t</sub> choices

bank.q: An NMOS inverter with a load has poor output high level and static current. Evaluate the four load choices and explain when a static CMOS inverter is preferred.
outline: resistive load has static current and ratio dependence
enhancement load loses V<sub>t</sub> at output high
pseudo-nMOS saves area but burns static power
static CMOS gives full levels and no steady-state current
choice depends on area, power and process

glossary.def: A complementary pair of one pMOS and one nMOS transistor that drives the output to V<sub>DD</sub> or ground.
The input voltage at which the inverter output equals the input, often written V<sub>M</sub>.
The voltage disturbance a logic gate can tolerate at its input without changing the interpreted output.
An inverter load made from a resistor connected between the supply and the output.
An nMOS load transistor that needs a gate voltage above its threshold to conduct.
An nMOS load transistor that conducts even when its gate-source voltage is zero.
A ratioed CMOS style with a pMOS pull-up that is always on and an nMOS pull-down network.
The time from a 50% input transition to the 50% output transition, averaged for high-to-low and low-to-high.
The total capacitance an inverter or gate must charge and discharge, including gate, diffusion and interconnect capacitance.
A number that compares the input capacitance of a gate with that of an inverter for the same output current.
The ratio of output capacitance to input capacitance for a logic stage, also called fanout.
The delay of a gate caused by its own internal capacitance when it drives no external load.
The product of logical effort, electrical effort and branching effort along a logic path.
Power used to charge and discharge capacitance, equal to α C V<sub>DD</sub><sup>2</sup> f.
Power dissipated when both nMOS and pMOS conduct during an input transition and current flows from supply to ground.
Current that flows between drain and source when the gate-source voltage is below the threshold voltage.
Tunnelling current through a thin gate oxide from gate to channel.
Reverse-bias current through drain and source p-n junctions.
A low-power method that disconnects idle blocks from the supply using high-threshold switch transistors.
A complementary logic style with pMOS pull-up and nMOS pull-down networks that gives full rail-to-rail outputs.
Logic whose output low level depends on the relative strength of a pull-up load and a pull-down network.
A MOS transistor used as a switch to pass a signal from input to output.
An nMOS and a pMOS in parallel that together pass both a strong 0 and a strong 1.
Clocked logic that precharges an output node and then evaluates a pull-down condition.
Dynamic logic with an inverter after each gate so cascaded stages can evaluate without false discharge.
Cascode voltage switch logic, a differential logic family with a cross-coupled pMOS pull-up latch.
